extracted.intended_audience: War Department / government contracting officers, quartermaster/subsistence/pay department officials, and legal advisors handling government bonds
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for formation, execution, evidence, sufficiency, acceptance, and liability of bonds (official bonds, contractors' bonds, and bonds for ordnance issued to educational institutions) under War Department regulation and statutes. Covers required documentary evidence, authorized signatories, penalty amounts, surety requirements, and when waivers or substitutions may be permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate as evidence of sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: A certificate when properly filled out and signed is the evidence of the present sufficiency of the bond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate should be acted on by the head of the bureau (approval or requiring a new bond) rather than referred to the Secretary of War; if a new bond is required the new bond is to be submitted to the Secretary for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with provision as to sufficiency of bond amount by bureau reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The provision relating to the sufficiency of the 'amount' of the bond is sufficiently complied with if the chief of each bureau reports twice a year to the Secretary a list of all bonds at least 18 months old including officer names, bond amounts, the greatest amounts of money liable to be handled by them during the succeeding 2.5 years, and recommends action (approve or fix new amount).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Secretary acts on the recommendation of the chief of bureau; where an inspector investigated sufficiency and recommended approval, the Secretary's approval of that recommendation constitutes compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of obligor's liability — duties vs subordinate custody
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a bond is conditioned that the obligor should 'carefully discharge the duties of his office or employment' and a subordinate (not selected/discharged by obligor) has personal custody of property, the obligor is required only to discharge his own duties, including supervision, and (if he does so) is not liable for loss from the subordinate's neglect or misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, where bond conditions refer to accounting for property 'intrusted to his care or custody,' obligor not liable for property not in his personal physical possession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bonds for contractors: statutory vs administrative nature and waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Giving bonds to secure performance of contracts for furnishing supplies/doing work for the War Department is generally a subject of administrative regulation and not required by statute (except where statute prescribes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary of War empowered to dispense with bonds in discretionary cases where statute does not specifically require them (e.g., small amounts, particular contract types).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of contract includes acceptance of required bond
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a bond is required for due performance of a contract, in absence of statute/regulation to contrary, the approval of the contract includes acceptance of the bond; additional written acceptance of the bond is not necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited authority: C. 22961, Mar. 24, 1908.

rubrics_metrics.name: No assignment of bond to contractor's creditors after completion
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no legal authority, after a contract has been completed, for assigning the bond to creditors of the contractor to enable them to sue on it in the name of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment to private creditors for their suit is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportionate reduction of penalty on partial completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a contract has been partly performed and a new bond is required because surety is no longer sufficient, the penalty may be proportionately reduced by reason of partial completion and by retained percentages held by the Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty amount regulation (10%–100%) and Secretary's waiver power
rubrics_metrics.description: Army Regulations provided that the amount of penalty in a contractor's bond will not be less than one-tenth nor more than the full amount of the consideration of the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where circumstances warrant, the Secretary may waive the regulatory requirement as to penalty amount and approve a smaller bond (example: very large contract with relatively small bond accepted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash deposit cannot substitute for statutory bond protecting labor/materialmen
rubrics_metrics.description: If statute requires a bond for the benefit of persons supplying labor/materials, a cash deposit in lieu of a bond cannot be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, where statute only requires a bond generally and the amount of penalty is a matter of regulation, the regulation as to penalty may be waived and an appropriate penalty fixed under the circumstances (e.g., remote locations where bonds are hard to secure). C. 29269, Nov. 29, 1911.

rubrics_metrics.name: No bond required for substitute contract when original bidder's guaranty absent
rubrics_metrics.description: If under a requirement a bidder must give a guaranty to enter into contract and furnish bond, and the bidder in default is replaced by another person, the statute does not require that the new contract entered into with the other person be accompanied by a bond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot require additional security where individual sureties fail financially
rubrics_metrics.description: Where sureties on a contractor's bond are individuals and one or more fail in financial responsibility so that bond is likely no longer good for required amount, there is no method by which additional security on that bond can be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for corporate officer to execute bond must be shown
rubrics_metrics.description: A bond executed in official capacity by the president or other officer of an incorporated college/university cannot be accepted as binding the corporation without evidence that the officer is legally empowered to act for and bind the institution (by act of incorporation or other evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: certified extract of minutes, charter copy; mere affidavit or uncertified certificate by secretary is generally insufficient unless small value or common knowledge justifies waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof that the signatory holds the office
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a bond purports to be signed by the president of the corporation, it should be shown (in connection with the bond) that the person so signing had been duly elected such president by the corporation or by a managing body authorized by the articles of incorporation to elect him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some cases (common knowledge of officers or very small values) proper evidence may be waived. C. 2366, June 21, 1910; C. 7666, Aug. 26, 1909.

rubrics_metrics.name: General/unspecific resolutions do not authorize execution of sealed bonds
rubrics_metrics.description: A board resolution empowering the president 'to negotiate and carry on any business which, in his judgment, tended to the welfare of the institution' or a by-law granting an executive committee 'general care' does not sufficiently authorize the execution of a sealed instrument such as a bond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific authority to execute bonds (or a general board authorization expressly covering such instruments) is required; otherwise bond will not be accepted. See P.39,158, Mar. 1, 1890; P.63,467, Feb. 10, 1894.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board authorization to execute bonds is sufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: A general authority from the board of trustees/board of regents to their president to execute such bonds as may be needed from time to time to secure ordnance stores is sufficient to authorize execution of bonds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticated minutes or transcript must accompany bond to prove authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Where trustees have authorized an officer to execute a bond, an extract of the minutes fully setting forth the adoption of the resolution should be furnished with the executed bond, certified by the secretary or custodian under the corporate seal; a mere certificate or affidavit of the secretary is not sufficient substitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only proper evidence of the proceedings of a body which keeps a record is the record itself or a duly authenticated transcript; omission may be waived for very small property values.

rubrics_metrics.name: If resolution omits officer's name, include record identifying signatory
rubrics_metrics.description: If a resolution authorizing the president to execute bonds does not give the name of the president, a copy of the record showing that the person whose name is signed as president was such officer should accompany the bond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A previously filed copy may be waived; example citations given where copies on file obviated repetition. (C. 768; C. 3104; etc.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Bond must be executed in correct legal name of corporation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a bond is executed by a corporation, the corporate name as signed must be the corporate name as given in the articles of incorporation expressed in full; where corporation exists as 'trustees' or 'board of trustees' the bond must be executed in that corporate name and not merely the institution's popular name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The corporate name in the body and signature of the bond should match; seal name should agree if impressed. (Multiple citations.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized officer must sign; authority cannot be improperly delegated
rubrics_metrics.description: The bond of a corporation must be signed for it by an officer of the corporation or some other person authorized to do so; where authority is vested in a board it may not be delegated to others unless articles permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An executive committee not recognized by the articles cannot validly delegate authority to execute bonds. Where articles permit, delegation specifics must be shown. (Numerous citations.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide certified copy of charter/articles to show capacity to bind
rubrics_metrics.description: A bond furnished by any incorporated college or university should be accompanied by a duly certified copy of the charter or articles of incorporation showing that the institution is a corporation and has power to enter into the obligation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copy should be authenticated by the certificate of the official custodian of the record (a U.S. commissioner certificate is ineffective). If county recorder has no seal, his official character should be certified by the custodian of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal may be corporation or individual depending on incorporation status
rubrics_metrics.description: Though bonds tendered under section 1225 R.S. have usually been in the name of the corporation, it is not essential that the corporation be the principal; a bond of an individual (e.g., president) may be accepted if security is sufficient; where college is not incorporated a personal bond should be required; where university is property of State the State is proper principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If institution lacks corporate capacity, do not accept bond in its name; require a properly authorized principal or personal bond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary's discretion on number/type of sureties
rubrics_metrics.description: No statutory form required by section 1225 R.S.; the Secretary of War may, if he deems the security ample, accept a bond with one surety or even accept the bond of the corporation without sureties, though generally safer to require sureties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sureties for colleges should in general be required to justify in the usual manner; exceptions exist for certain principals like city trustees where sureties might be dispensed with. (P.59,176; C.768; C.2366.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting indemnity/security company bond in place of usual bond
rubrics_metrics.description: A bond of indemnity of a security company where the company would be the only obligor might, in the Secretary's discretion, be accepted in place of the usual bond given under section 1225 R.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance should not, per se, release the college from its liability as bailee; instrument should be executed to leave no question that bailee liability continues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bond must accurately state statutory capacities/recitals (e.g., student capacity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where statute requires bonds to state a college's capacity (e.g., capacity to educate 150 male students), a bond that recites a lesser capacity (e.g., 80) is defective and not legally acceptable; it should specifically state the capacity required by the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bond penalty must not exceed authority given by corporate resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: If the penalty of the bond as offered is greater than the sum for which the president (or other officer) was authorized by a board resolution to give bond, the bond cannot be accepted and a new bond should be furnished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given where off-by-small-amount exceeded authorization and bond rejected. (P.35,82; C.3543.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligor and sureties must be bound without condition or reservation
rubrics_metrics.description: The obligor and sureties should be bound in the bond without condition or reservation; a provision that recourse should be had to college property before sureties' property is resorted to makes bond unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bond penalty relative to ordnance value — double value rule and substantial compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations require that the bond given to secure safe-keeping of ordnance stores shall be in double the value of the stores issued; accepting a bond in excess of double value is permissible to cover future issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A bond lacking a small shortfall (e.g., $20) of being double the value may be treated as defective; a bond lacking a trivial amount (e.g., 55 cents) has been held substantial compliance — discretion applies. (C.942; C.950; C.1766.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct recitation whether stores 'have been issued' or 'to be issued'
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a bond recites that certain ordnance stores 'have been issued' whereas it was intended to cover stores not yet issued, the language should be changed to 'to be issued.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the bond fails to state whether stores have been issued or are to be issued (left blank), the omission may be waived in some cases. (C.1828; C.1711.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary's authority under section 1191 to decide sufficiency of sureties
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1191 R.S. requires officers of certain departments to give bonds 'in such sums as the Secretary of War may direct'; by implication the Secretary has power to decide sufficiency of sureties and may accept security companies as sureties on such bonds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Held reasonable that Congress did not intend to divide duties of passing on bonds; Secretary may accept security companies as sureties. (P.50,118.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required for corporate surety officers' authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations regarding corporate sureties require filing with the War Department copies of the record of the selection and qualification of the officers and copies of by-laws or records authorizing certain officers to execute bonds; a mere certificate by 'A, secretary' that 'B is the president and A is the secretary' is not proper evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defect may be waived by the War Department where the value of the property is small (example: $113.97). (C.1482; C.3946; C.7666.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Surety liability independent of payment of premiums; no unilateral cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: A corporate surety continues to be bound by a bond notwithstanding the principal's failure to pay premiums agreed upon; attempts by the surety to cancel the bond have no legal effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liability of the surety continues until contract is satisfied by performance or payment of damages for breach; U.S. has no interest in premium arrangements between principal and surety. (C.8553; C.12359.)
